title: How the Martel band read and arranged
summary: Old Man Martel bought lead sheets, wrote a lead for Bert, and the band played ensemble with everyone improvising around it.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So this Martel Band was the first actual band other than the family band that you worked with on a regular basis.
A regular, organized, pretty good band.
Darensbourg - 51
Did they read?
Well, all of them could read some.
But did they read, I mean, on a job?

Well, they didn't read too much. What would have happened... But Old Man Martel was a good musician. He would buy a lead sheet of the leading tunes. For instance, the first time I ever played "Sand" in my life was with him. He would buy the lead sheet. And he would write, write a part for Bert, a trumpet part. And I don't think he ever wrote anything for Dayton. I think he would write the chords down for Hillary and...
Usually he played B-flat soprano.
Yes.
Well, if he bought the part, what would he write for the trumpet? It would be the same part, but...
He'd write the lead.
So they wouldn't play in unison.
No. They'd doodle around there in some kind of way. Ensemble. It was all ensemble, you know.
I wanted to ask you about that...

And I did... I noodled around with that soprano and everything. It was a funny thing. Everybody played something different. Bert was the trumpet, but he'd play, he was making his little figurations over there, and
Old Man Martel would be wailing there on the lead. He played lead all the time. A strong lead.
So in other words, the part he would write for Bert, the trumpet player, wouldn't be the lead. It would be some figuration or something.
Yes.
And he would play the lead (is that what you're saying?) on the B-flat soprano.

No, no. He'd write Bert a lead, too. I don't think he was even that good a musician where he could really write the harmony like a little arrangement. But he would write Bert a lead, and Bert would learn the lead, just for him to have a part. Because he could have just as well the B-flat soprano part.
That's what I'm saying.
They didn't do that.
But they didn't play in unison then.
No. Bert would get that part and learn that lead, and then he would improvise off of that.
